questions.stem: Which of the following is a prime number?
questions.solution: The number 29 is a prime number because it has only two factors, 1 and itself. 15, 21, and 27 are not prime because they have more than two factors.

questions.stem: What is the prime factorisation of 30?
questions.solution: The correct answer is 2 × 3 × 5. Prime factorisation is the process of breaking a number into its prime number components. 30 can be divided by 2, resulting in 15. 15 can be divided by 3, resulting in 5. Finally, 5 is a prime number. Therefore, the prime factorisation of 30 is 2 × 3 × 5.

hi.solution: सही उत्तर 2 × 3 × 5 है। अभाज्य गुणनखंड एक संख्या के अभाज्य संख्या घटकों में विभाजन की प्रक्रिया है। 30 को 2 से विभाजित किया जा सकता है, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप 15 प्राप्त होता है। 15 को 3 से विभाजित किया जा सकता है, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप 5 प्राप्त होता है। अंत में, 5 एक अभाज्य संख्या है। इसलिए, 30 का अभाज्य गुणनखंड 2 × 3 × 5 है।
hi.critique: The Hindi translation is accurate, maintains the same meaning, and uses appropriate mathematical terminology.

questions.stem: If the number formed by the last three digits of a number is divisible by 8, then the original number is also divisible by 8. Which of the following numbers is divisible by 8?
questions.solution: The number 8560 is divisible by 8 because the last three digits, 560, are divisible by 8. 8564, 8568, and 8572 are not divisible by 8 because their last three digits are not divisible by 8.

hi.solution: संख्या 8560, 8 से विभाज्य है क्योंकि अंतिम तीन अंक 560, 8 से विभाज्य हैं। 8564, 8568 और 8572, 8 से विभाज्य नहीं हैं क्योंकि इनके अंतिम तीन अंक 8 से विभाज्य नहीं हैं।

questions.stem: If the prime factorisation of the first number is 2 × 3 × 7 and the second number is 3 × 7 × 11, are they co-prime?
choices: Yes, the first number is divisible by the second
No, the second number is divisible by the first
questions.solution: The correct answer is No, they are not co-prime. Co-prime numbers have no common prime factors. Both numbers share the prime factors 3 and 7, so they are not co-prime. The first number is not divisible by the second, and the second is not divisible by the first, because the second has an extra prime factor (11) not present in the first. The misconception might be thinking that if the prime factors are in the same order, the numbers are co-prime, or that the presence of some common prime factors does not matter.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of numbers are safe (co-prime) and have no common factor other than 1?
questions.solution: The pair 4 and 9 are co-prime because they have no common factors other than 1. The other pairs have common factors: 15 and 39 share 3, 18 and 29 share 1 but are not co-prime, and 20 and 55 share 5. Co-prime numbers have no common factor other than 1, so 4 and 9 are the only pair that satisfies this condition.
